label: History
value: Dorothy wound Tiktok up again under his left arm.
unit: Tiktok befriended Dorothy Gale and saved both her life and Billina's life during past adventures. Later, Princess Ozma observed Dorothy traveling toward the Country of the Winkies in her magic picture. Because Ozma was busy preparing for her grand birthday celebration in the Emerald City, she dispatched Tiktok and Billina to welcome Dorothy and her companions. Upon meeting Dorothy's new companions—the shaggy man, Polly, and Button-Bright—Tiktok bowed politely, but his speech mechanism ran down mid-sentence, requiring Dorothy to wind him up under his right arm. Shortly afterward, his thought mechanism ran down, causing him to utter unintelligible babble until Dorothy wound him up again under his left arm. Once fully restored, Tiktok successfully conveyed Princess Ozma's invitation for Dorothy and her friends to proceed directly to the Emerald City.

label: History
value: Polychrome is the Daughter of the Rainbow
unit: Button-Bright was found sitting under a chestnut tree along a remote road, steadily digging a hole with a piece of wood. When questioned by Dorothy Gale and the Shaggy Man, he could not explain where he lived or how he got there, leading them to realize he was lost. Because of the Shaggy Man's Love Magnet, Button-Bright willingly joined the party on their journey. Upon encountering the fox-soldiers of Foxville, his innocent questioning led the fox-captain to consider him clever, and he was brought before King Dox. During their travels, he was temporarily transformed into having a fox's head by King Dox before later having his true face restored at the Truth Pond. Along the way, he met Polychrome, the Daughter of the Rainbow, and eventually reached the Emerald City. In the royal palace, he was welcomed by Princess Ozma and Glinda the Good, assisted in winding up Tik-Tok, and enthusiastically attended Princess Ozma's royal birthday feast.

label: Personality
value: The Woggle-Bug displays humility when reprimanded by his companions.
unit: The Woggle-Bug is intensely proud of his high level of education and vast erudition, frequently boasting that he is the most intelligent being in Oz. He considers himself a cultured gentleman, making polite bows and striving to impress others with his learning. He takes great pleasure in surprising people, strutting about after making brilliant remarks, and indulging in irresistible wordplays and puns. Despite his pomposity and tendency to display rudeness or condescending behavior, he displays humility when reprimanded or threatened by his companions.

label: History
value: At the Tin Woodman's palace, the Scarecrow's clothes were pressed.
unit: The Scarecrow set out on a journey along the yellow brick road to seek brains from the Wizard of Oz in the Emerald City, joining Dorothy Gale on her quest to return to Kansas. Along the way, he welcomed the Tin Woodman into their traveling party and survived encounters with the Stinging Bees and Winged Monkeys sent by the Wicked Witch. He eventually became the monarch of the Emerald City, wearing a heavy golden crown and ruling from his throne. Upon meeting Jack Pumpkinhead, he believed they spoke different languages and called for an interpreter until he realized Jack's smiling mouth was carved that way. After being driven out of the Emerald City by rebels, he traveled with Tip and Jack Pumpkinhead upon the live Saw-Horse to seek aid from his friend, the Tin Woodman. At the Tin Woodman's palace, the Scarecrow's head was laundered and restuffed with his original brains, his clothes were pressed, and his crown was re-stitched before he set out to recapture the Emerald City.

label: History
value: King Dox rules over the city of Foxville
unit: King Dox rules over the civilized city of Foxville as King Renard the Fourth. When Dorothy Gale, Button-Bright, the shaggy man, and Toto are brought into his city by his fox-soldiers, he receives them in his palace. Finding Button-Bright's answers remarkably clever, King Dox uses his magic to transform Button-Bright's human head into a fox head, later claiming he lacks the power to undo the change. He hosts the travelers for a rich dinner of poultry and takes them to a local theater performance acted by foxes dressed in feathered costumes. During their stay, he expresses his hatred for Aesop's fables for portraying foxes as cruel. Learning that Dorothy is a friend of Princess Ozma, King Dox asks her to procure an invitation for him to attend Ozma's upcoming birthday celebration. After receiving an invitation, he journeys across the desert to the Land of Oz and attends the royal gathering in the Emerald City, where he strutted around the Throne-Room and knelt at Dorothy's feet upon learning she is a Princess of Oz.

I am sorry to say that no one had ever told the little boy much about fairies of any kind; this being the case, it is easy to understand how much this strange experience startled and astonished him.

value: When Jim lost, he kicked the Sawhorse in anger.
unit: Zeb fell into a subterranean realm alongside Dorothy, his horse Jim, and the Wizard following an earthquake. Together, they navigated through various strange underground worlds, surviving attacks by Gargoyles and facing judgment in distant kingdoms. After escaping the subterranean regions, they safely arrived in the Land of Oz. Upon reaching the Emerald City's Royal Palace, Zeb unharnessed Jim and bathed before changing into a velvet costume to dine with Princess Ozma. During the royal games, he competed in a wrestling match against a strong Munchkin who easily defeated him, and then engaged in a boxing match that caused the Munchkin to cry. Later, Zeb served as the starter for a race between Jim and the Sawhorse, calling the signal to begin. When Jim lost and kicked the Sawhorse in anger, Zeb rushed over to warn his horse to control his temper before the royal beasts could harm him. Following the festivities, he accompanied Jim back to the city while discussing their place in a fairy land.

label: History
value: The Nome King placed magical enchantments on Evardo's mother.
unit: Evardo was born as the eldest prince of the royal family of Ev. His father, the King, sold Evardo, his mother, and his nine siblings to the Nome King, who placed them under magical enchantments as ornaments in his subterranean palace. label: History
value: Mombi raised Tip as her ward.
unit: Mombi lived on a round farm in the Gillikin Country, where she was widely suspected by the local inhabitants of practicing illegal magic arts. In the past, she was secretly visited three times by the Wizard of Oz, who gave her the infant Princess Ozma to hide. In return, Mombi learned various magical tricks from the Wizard and transformed the young princess into a boy named Tip, whom she raised as her ward while forcing him to perform hard chores on her farm. Upon obtaining the Powder of Life from a crooked mountain wizard, Mombi tested the magical powder on Jack Pumpkinhead—a wooden dummy created by Tip to scare her—and brought the figure to life. After Tip escaped her farm, Mombi traveled to the Emerald City to assist General Jinjur and her rebel army. When Glinda surrounded the city demanding Mombi's surrender, Mombi attempted to deceive her by magically swapping forms with Jellia Jamb and later transforming herself into a red rose in the palace garden. Her trick was ultimately exposed when the Tin Woodman plucked the rose, leading to her capture. Brought before Glinda, Mombi was forced to speak the absolute truth under threat of death or the loss of her powers, confessing that she had transformed Princess Ozma into Tip.

value: Its body rocks sidewise as it walks.
unit: The Saw-Horse is an artificial, quadrupedal wooden creature constructed like a carpenter's saw-horse. Its legs are stiff and lack knee-joints, causing its body to rock sidewise in a cradle-like pacing motion as it walks. It has knotty, bulging eyes, a short post hammered into its back to serve as a handhold, ears whittled out of tree bark, and legs shod with plates of gold.

passages.v02:c07:p0000: The Saw-Horse, finding himself alive, seemed even more astonished than Tip. He rolled his knotty eyes from side to side, taking a first wondering view of the world in which he had now so important an existence. Then he tried to look at himself; but he had, indeed, no neck to turn; so that in the endeavor to see his body he kept circling around and around, without catching even a glimpse of it. His legs were stiff and awkward, for there were no knee-joints in them; so that presently he bumped against Jack Pumpkinhead and sent that personage tumbling upon the moss that lined the roadside.
passages.v02:c07:p0011: It was really comical to see the creature walk; for it moved the legs on its right side together, and those on its left side together, as a pacing horse does; and that made its body rock sidewise, like a cradle.
passages.v02:c07:p0012: Tip patted it upon the head, and said “Good boy! Good Boy!” in a coaxing tone; and the Saw-Horse pranced away to examine with its bulging eyes the form of Jack Pumpkinhead.
passages.v02:c07:p0018: So Tip got out his knife and fashioned some ears out of the bark of a small tree.
passages.v02:c07:p0057: “I’ll fix it!” said he, at length. He went into the wood and cut a short length of limb from a young, stout tree. One end of this he sharpened to a point, and then he dug a hole in the back of the Saw-Horse, just behind its head. Next he brought a piece of rock from the road and hammered the post firmly into the animal’s back.
passages.v04:c19:p0049: "Princess Ozma did that," was the reply; "and it saves my legs from wearing out. We've had a good many adventures together, Ozma and I, and she likes me."

screen.reason: The passage explicitly states that the Saw-Horse's body rocks sidewise as it walks.

label: Princess Ozma
value: Parent of — Reared Ozma from infancy after transforming her into the boy Tip.

passages.v02:c03:p0001: This boy remembered nothing of his parents, for he had been brought when quite young to be reared by the old woman known as Mombi, whose reputation, I am sorry to say, was none of the best. For the Gillikin people had reason to suspect her of indulging in magical arts, and therefore hesitated to associate with her.
passages.v02:c25:p0044: “The Wizard brought to me the girl Ozma, who was then no more than a baby, and begged me to conceal the child.”
passages.v02:c25:p0052: “Into a boy!” said Mombi, in a low tone.
passages.v02:c25:p0053: “A boy!” echoed every voice; and then, because they knew that this old woman had reared Tip from childhood, all eyes were turned to where the boy stood.
passages.v02:c25:p0054: “Yes,” said the old Witch, nodding her head; “that is the Princess Ozma—the child brought to me by the Wizard who stole her father’s throne. That is the rightful ruler of the Emerald City!” and she pointed her long bony finger straight at the boy.

label: Personality
value: Dorothy values good behavior in her pets
unit: Dorothy is sweet, brave, resourceful, and compassionate, maintaining a steadfast, affectionate heart through all her queer journeys. She demonstrates deep care and concern for her friends and pets, comforting those in distress and acting as a protective guide. She readily offers friendship to strangers she encounters, though she can occasionally get provoked when companions give silly or useless answers. She values good behavior in her pets and politely respects royal customs.

passages.v03:c12:p0000: The first thing Dorothy did was to rush into the embrace of the Scarecrow, whose painted face beamed with delight as he pressed her form to his straw-padded bosom. Then the Tin Woodman embraced her—very gently, for he knew his tin arms might hurt her if he squeezed too roughly.
passages.v03:c12:p0007: In an instant Dorothy was hugging the huge Lion joyfully.
passages.v03:c12:p0020: "I think you are a very good tiger," said Dorothy, patting the huge head of the beast.
